# r4.4

- Fixes automatic updates being stopped solely by advisory Restart Manager file-use reports. Actual sharing locks are retried for a bounded period; ownership, signature, settings and process checks remain enforced.
- Prepares the new Nearly.exe in an update subfolder on the same volume, then replaces the live filename in one native rename. Retains the verified previous version and removes the deliberate missing-executable gap between two separate renames.
- Automatically restores the verified previous version after a definite failure to start the new process. Uncertain process or journal outcomes are not blindly retried. Startup also allows a short handoff interval for a finishing update helper.
- Allows the manual installer to recover an owned installation with unfinished update state. After successful installation it archives the pinned recovery-state directory without overwriting existing evidence, while preserving settings. It no longer requires manual deletion of hidden recovery folders for this case.
- Keeps stable-release update checks, the Update now / Later choice, future-launch reminders after Later, prerelease exclusion, and automatic cleanup of downloaded installers after success. Manually supplied installers are retained.

## Updating from an older version

The first automatic update still uses the helper from the currently installed version. These fixes cannot change an old helper already running. If an update is blocked, download this installer and reinstall into the same installation folder; settings are preserved.

## Verification and limits

Generated Windows tests cover 48 apply and 48 restore interruption boundaries, live-filename preservation, retained backups, real sharing locks, helper handoff, and automatic rollback after definite launch failure. Installer contracts and NSIS compilation are checked. This is not a guarantee against every power failure, reboot, filesystem fault or concurrent writer. Unrecoverable interrupted state can still require manual reinstall, and an installer failure after writing files is not an atomic rollback.

Actual manual-reinstall repair, native dialog presentation, genuine reboot/power-loss recovery and a signed end-to-end installed update of this change have not been qualified. The release workflow validates builds, tests and signatures without installing on the developer's computer.

Stable release, replacing r4.3 as Latest. Uses the existing application registration, settings and normal updater channel.
